observed_original_abi.calling_convention_observation: Receiver is consumed from ECX (0x004adaa4: MOV [EBP-4],ECX) and no stack argument is read, so the observed port is receiver-in-ECX. The terminal instruction is a bare RET (0x004adab0: c3) with no immediate, which proves the callee pops zero stack words. Both cdecl and thiscall produce the same nine bytes for this body; thiscall is recorded because every observed call site loads ECX immediately before the call (0x0043e433 / 0x004a077d / MOV ECX,[EBP-0x50] then CALL 0x004adaa0).
observed_original_abi.return_semantics: the single-precision value stored at receiver + 0x38, unmodified
observed_original_abi.return_observation: 0x004adaaa: D9 40 38 (FLD float ptr [EAX + 0x38]) is the only value-producing instruction; the frame teardown at 0x004adaad..0x004adab0 (MOV ESP,EBP; POP EBP; RET) touches no FP register, so ST0 survives to the caller.
observed_original_abi.hidden_receiver: ECX, spilled to [EBP-0x4] at 0x004adaa4 and reloaded at 0x004adaa7
observed_original_abi.x87_stack_effect: pushes exactly one value and pops none; the caller owns the matching pop

layout.frame: PUSH EBP / MOV EBP,ESP / PUSH ECX / MOV ESP,EBP / POP EBP. 4 bytes of locals ([EBP-4]) used only to spill the receiver. No register save/restore, no SUB ESP.
layout.reads: exactly one 4-byte read: the float at receiver + 0x38. No global, no other field, no stack argument, no callee.

observed_mechanics: 0x004adaa0: PUSH EBP / 0x004adaa1: MOV EBP,ESP -- standard frame, two instructions, no size adjustment
0x004adaa3: PUSH ECX / 0x004adaa4: MOV dword ptr [EBP - 0x4],ECX -- the receiver is spilled to a frame slot rather than kept in a callee-saved register, so nothing needs restoring
0x004adaa7: MOV EAX,dword ptr [EBP - 0x4] -- reloads the receiver; this is the only reason the spill exists
0x004adaaa: FLD float ptr [EAX + 0x38] -- d9 40 38. The disp8 is +0x38; this is the only memory operand in the body and there is no null test on EAX beforehand
0x004adaad: MOV ESP,EBP / 0x004adaaf: POP EBP -- frame teardown, no FP instruction, so ST0 is the return value
0x004adab0: RET -- c3, no immediate, so the callee pops zero stack words

semantic_contract: Return the single-precision field at receiver + 0x38 and nothing else. The body is a single unguarded FLD; there is no null check, no default value, no side effect, no global access and no callee. The receiver is the sub-object that its callers hold at +0x28 of their own argument, and at least one caller null-checks that pointer before the call, which is why the absence of a check here is safe in the observed build rather than an oversight. The x87 stack is pushed once and never popped by this function, so the caller owns the matching pop.
classification_rationale: The behaviour is not in doubt: one 4-byte float load at +0x38, returned in ST0, established by the disassembly, the live bytes, and the mirror-image setter at 0x004ada80. It is not STRONG_SEMANTIC because a material element is bounded rather than established: the OWNING TYPE is unknown. No vtable for the receiver was located, the binary carries no RTTI, and no Spore-ModAPI class with a float at +0x38 matches the 26 observed callers. The name 'getter for a float at +0x38' is therefore structural, and any SDK spelling for it would be a guess. It is not STRUCTURAL_ONLY because a real behavioural claim (an unconditional, un-defaulted field read) is supported here, not just a layout.
semantic_findings: 0x004adaa0 is an unconditional accessor for a 32-bit float at receiver + 0x38; the whole body is 17 bytes and 9 instructions.
The +0x38 field is a float and not a bit pattern because 0x004ada80 stores to the same offset with MOVSS, giving a matched get/set pair.
The x87 return is real: no FP instruction appears in the epilogue, so ST0 survives the frame teardown.
There is no null check in the callee. The only null check observed is in the caller (0x004a076e), so the missing check is the caller's contract, not an omission recovered from a decompiler.
It sits in a five-member accessor family (0x004ada40, 0x004ada80, 0x004adaa0, 0x004adac0, 0x004adae0); the +0x3c and +0x40 setters use plain MOV, so only +0x38 is proven to be a float.
Callers treat the answer purely numerically: one multiplies it by a .rdata constant (0x013eb960) and one divides it by 20.0f (0x013eecd8). Nothing tests it as a predicate.
The receiver is always reached as the +0x28 sub-object of the caller's own argument, so the accessor's own type is a sub-object, not the top-level object the callers hold.
unresolved_questions: What class owns the +0x38 float? No vtable was located for the receiver type and the binary has no RTTI, so the owner is unnamed.
What does the float mean (scale, radius, alpha, weight, time)? Every inspected consumer only multiplies or divides it by a constant, which is compatible with all of those.
Why is there no getter for +0x3c or +0x40 when both have setters? Either the getters were inlined at every use or they do not exist; the binary cannot distinguish these.
The 26 caller fan-in is dominated by four functions in the 0x0043xxxx-0x004axxxx range with no subsystem attribution. Their relationship to the owning type is not established.
What are the float constants at 0x013eb960 (0x3c23d70a) and 0x013eecd8 (0x41a00000 = 20.0f)? 20.0f is self-evident; the other is not, and neither is named in the SDK.
Is 0x004adaa0 also a vtable entry? A pointer scan of the target's address was not performed, so only direct-call sites are recorded.
confidence_note: confidence in the per-aspect claim, not a probability of behavioural equivalence with any shipped source
